question: Which picture mode is the easiest on the eyes, and where do I select it?
answer:
The easiest-on-the-eyes mode is “Natural,” which reduces eye strain for a comfortable viewing experience [p0001].

To select it:
1) Go to Settings > Picture > Picture Mode.
2) Choose Natural. [p0001]
reference_answer: Select Natural in Settings > Picture > Picture Mode. It reduces eye strain for a comfortable viewing experience. The function may not be supported depending on the model.

question: How do I change the picture size?
answer:
Here’s how to change the picture size on your Smart Tech TV:

1) Open the menu
- Go to: Settings > Picture > Picture Size Settings > Picture Size [p0020]

2) Choose a size
- Options: 16:9 Standard, Custom, or 4:3 [p0020]
  - Note: Avoid watching in 4:3 for long periods to prevent after images. Screen burn from such use isn’t covered for commercial/non‑consumer use [p0020].
  - Supported sizes can vary by input signal [p0020].

3) Fit the image to the screen (if available)
- Go to: Settings > Picture > Picture Size Settings > Fit to Screen [p0118]
  - This may be unavailable depending on your current Picture Size setting or the broadcast signal [p0118].

4) Adjust zoom/position (only when using Custom)
- Go to: Settings > Picture > Picture Size Settings > Zoom and Position [p0019]
  - Available only if Picture Size is set to Custom [p0019].
  - For analog channels, first enlarge the picture, then adjust position [p0019].

If any of these options are grayed out, it’s due to the current input signal or picture size selection [p0020][p0118]. Would you like help choosing the best option for your source device?
reference_answer: Open Settings > Picture > Picture Size Settings > Picture Size and choose a size: 16:9 Standard, Custom or 4:3. Do not watch in 4:3 mode for long periods, because the black bars can leave temporary or permanent after-images. The supported sizes depend on the input signal.
must_include: Settings > Picture > Picture Size Settings > Picture Size; options 16:9 Standard, Custom, 4:3

question: My screen is black but I can still hear the sound. What should I do?
answer:
Here are all the checks to fix a black screen while sound still plays:

1) Confirm the correct source
- Press Source on the remote and make sure the active input is correct (HDMI, TV, etc.). [p0223]

2) Disable power saving and screen-off states
- Go to Settings > General > Eco Solution > Power Saving Mode = Off. [p0223]
- Check Settings > Picture > Expert Settings and ensure Backlight is not set extremely low. [p0223]
- If you were playing media, make sure “Picture Off” is not active. Also exit Ambient Mode if it may be showing a black state. [p0223]

3) Run the Picture Test
- Go to Settings > Support > Self Diagnosis > Start Picture Test. [p0223]
- If the test picture appears: the TV is fine; the issue is the connected device or cable. Re-seat or replace the HDMI cable, or check the external device. [p0223]
- If the test picture stays black while sound works: power-cycle the TV by unplugging it for 60 seconds, plug back in, and test again. Then contact support if still black (possible backlight fault). [p0223]

If you’d like, I can hand you over to a human colleague for further help, especially if the Picture Test is black after a power-cycle.
reference_answer: Check that the right input is selected in Source, set Settings > General > Eco Solution > Power Saving Mode to Off, and run Settings > Support > Self Diagnosis > Start Picture Test. If the test picture appears, the connected device or its cable is the cause. Unplug the TV for 60 seconds and connect it again. Contact support if the Picture Test stays black while the sound works.
must_include: check the input in Source; Power Saving Mode off; Start Picture Test (Settings > Support > Self Diagnosis); unplug for 60 seconds; contact support if the test stays black
unknown_menu_paths: Settings > General > Eco Solution > Power Saving Mode = Off

question: Sports and action scenes look blurry. How can I improve this?
answer:
Here are the checks and fixes to improve motion clarity on your Smart Tech TV:

1) Choose a suitable Picture Mode
- Go to Settings > Picture > Picture Mode.
- Select Movie or Standard. These modes reduce aggressive processing that can cause smearing in fast motion. [p0226]

2) Adjust motion settings
- Go to Settings > Picture > Expert Settings > Auto Motion Settings.
- Try the available options and test during a fast scene to see which looks cleanest (reduce blur/ghosting without adding artifacts). [p0226]

3) Run a picture self test
- Go to Settings > Support > Self Diagnosis > Start Picture Test.
- If the test image is sharp, the TV is fine and the source/broadcast is likely the cause. [p0226]

4) Check signal quality
- Go to Settings > Support > Self Diagnosis > Signal Information to review signal strength/quality.
- Weak or highly compressed signals can cause blur and artifacts, especially in sports. [p0226][p0117]

5) Prefer higher‑quality sources
- Watch HD channels or higher-quality streams when available. Compressed content (often sports) can look blurry regardless of TV settings. [p0226][p0117]
- Note: Images may look blurry depending on the service provider’s circumstances. [p0166]

6) If you changed many settings
- Go to Settings > Picture > Expert Settings > Reset Picture to return to defaults and then apply only the changes above. [p0226]

Did these steps improve motion clarity? If not, I can hand you over to a human colleague for further assistance.
reference_answer: Select Movie or Standard in Settings > Picture > Picture Mode and try the options in Settings > Picture > Expert Settings > Auto Motion Settings. Run Start Picture Test: if the test picture is sharp, the TV is fine and the broadcast is the cause, so check Signal Information and choose HD channels where possible. Use Reset Picture if you changed many settings.
must_include: Movie or Standard picture mode; Auto Motion Settings; Start Picture Test: if the test picture is sharp the broadcast is the cause, so check Signal Information and choose HD channels; Reset Picture if many settings were changed
unknown_menu_paths: Settings > Support > Self Diagnosis > Signal Information to review signal strength/quality | Settings > Picture > Expert Settings > Reset Picture to return to defaults

question: Can I update software through internet and through USB device?
answer:
Yes. You can update either way:

1) Through the Internet
- Go to: Settings > Support > Software Update > Update Now.
- Keep the TV powered on until it restarts by itself. An active Internet connection is required. Note: video and audio settings reset to defaults after an update. [p0177]

2) Through a USB device
- On a computer, download the update package from the Smart Tech website (smarttech-inc.example).
- Save the file in the USB drive’s top-level (root) folder.
- Plug the USB into the TV, then go to: Settings > Support > Software Update > Update Now.
- Do not turn off the TV during the update; it will restart when finished. [p0177]

Optional: You can also enable automatic Internet updates in Settings > Support > Software Update > Auto Update. This applies updates in the background and finalizes them the next time the TV is turned on. Requires Internet; app updates are separate in APPS > Settings. [p0007]
reference_answer: Yes. Through the Internet: Settings > Support > Software Update > Update Now (needs an active Internet connection). Through a USB device: download the update package from the Smart Tech website, save it in the top-level folder of the USB device (otherwise the TV cannot find it), connect the device and update. Do not turn the TV off during the update. Video and audio settings are reset to their defaults afterwards.
must_include: Settings > Support > Software Update > Update Now; USB update: package from the website in the top-level folder; do not switch the TV off

question: An app asks me to sign in again every time I open it. How do I stop that?
answer:
Here are the steps to stop an app from asking you to sign in every time:

1) Set the TV’s clock to automatic
- Go to: Settings > General > System Manager > Time > Clock > Clock Mode
- Set Clock Mode to Auto [p0231]

2) Make sure you’re signed in to your Smart Tech account on the TV
- Go to: Settings > General > System Manager > Smart Tech Account > Sign In
- Sign in if you’re signed out [p0231]

3) Re-authenticate inside the app
- Open the app, sign out, then sign in again
- Keep the “stay signed in” or similar box ticked if shown [p0231]

4) Reinstall the app
- In APPS, delete the app and install it again [p0231]

5) Reset Smart Tech Hub (last resort)
- Go to: Settings > Support > Self Diagnosis > Reset Smart Tech Hub
- Note: this deletes account information, service agreements, and apps [p0231]

If the app also signs you out on other devices, contact the app provider, as it may be ending sessions on their side [p0231]. If you want, I can hand you over to a human colleague for further help.
reference_answer: Set the clock to automatic in Settings > General > System Manager > Time, check the sign-in in Settings > General > System Manager > Smart Tech Account > Sign In, and sign out and in again inside the app. If it continues, delete the app in APPS and install it again. Reset Smart Tech Hub is a last step: it deletes account information and apps.
must_include: set the clock to Auto (Time > Clock > Clock Mode); check Smart Tech Account > Sign In; sign out and in inside the app; reinstall the app; Reset Smart Tech Hub only as a last step

question: The TV keeps showing the software update message even after I updated. What can I do?
answer:
Here’s how to stop repeated software update prompts:

1) Verify network and finish the update
- Go to Settings > General > Network > Network Status to confirm the TV is online [p0233].
- Then run the updater: Settings > Support > Software Update > Update Now. Let it complete, and do not turn off the TV; it will restart itself when done [p0233][p0177].

2) Ensure enough storage
- Delete unused apps to free space, then run Update Now again [p0233].

3) Update via USB (bypasses network/storage issues)
- On a computer, download the latest TV software from the Smart Tech website (smarttech-inc.example).
- Copy the update package to the USB drive’s top-level folder (not inside any folder) [p0177].
- Plug the USB into the TV and go to Settings > Support > Software Update > Update Now to install. Do not power off; the TV will turn off/on automatically. Note: video/audio settings reset to defaults after an update [p0177].

4) Optional: manage automatic updates
- If desired, toggle Settings > Support > Software Update > Auto Update on/off. Requires Internet; apps update separately in APPS > Settings [p0007].

If the message appears again after a successful update and the version in Settings > Support > About This TV does not change, please let me hand you over to a human colleague for further assistance [p0233].
reference_answer: Open Settings > Support > Software Update > Update Now and let the update finish without switching the TV off. Check Network Status and free storage first. You can also update from a USB device with the package from the Smart Tech website. If the message returns and the version in Settings > Support > About This TV does not change, contact support.
must_include: Software Update > Update Now and do not switch off; check Network Status and free storage; USB update; contact support if the version does not change
unknown_menu_paths: Settings > General > Network > Network Status to confirm the TV is online [p0233] | Settings > Support > Software Update > Update Now to install | Settings > Support > Software Update > Auto Update on/off

question: How do I switch the TV to my Blu-ray player?
answer:
Here are all the ways supported by your TV to switch to a Blu-ray player:

1) Using HDMI (recommended)
- Connect the Blu-ray player to an HDMI port on the TV and turn the player on. [p0006]
- Switch input: Press Source on the remote and select the HDMI port your player is connected to. The player’s output will display. [p0006]
- Auto-switch (if supported): When you turn on the Blu-ray player, the TV may switch to that HDMI input automatically. [p0006]
- Optional: Set up Universal Remote so the TV remote can control the player. Point the TV remote at the player and follow the on‑screen prompts when detected. [p0006]

2) Using Component (only if your model has COMPONENT IN / AV IN)
- Connect the player’s Component OUT to the TV’s COMPONENT IN / AV IN using the provided blue component adapter and yellow AV adapter. Match colors (blue to blue, green to green, red to red, etc.). Both adapters must be connected for component video to work. Supports up to 1080p. [p0053]
- Switch input: Press Source and select the Component/AV input. [p0053]

Notes
- If you connected the player by USB (for media files), a pop‑up may appear to access media content. This does not control Blu‑ray video playback; use HDMI or Component for that. [p0006]
- DVD/Blu‑ray subtitles are controlled on the player, not by the TV’s caption feature. [p0101]

If you don’t see the player listed under Source, tell me how it’s connected (HDMI port number or Component) and what you see on screen, and I can help further.
reference_answer: Open Source and select the connected device (here the Blu-ray player). The output of the selected device is then displayed on the TV screen.
must_include: open Source; select the connected device

question: How do I connect a Bluetooth keyboard to the TV?
answer:
Here’s how to connect a Bluetooth keyboard to your Smart Tech TV:

1) Put the keyboard in Bluetooth pairing mode and place it close to the TV. [p0241]  
2) On the TV, go to: Settings > General > External Device Manager > Input Device Manager > Bluetooth Device List. [p0176][p0179]  
3) If the keyboard doesn’t appear, select Refresh to scan again and keep the keyboard nearby. [p0176]  
4) Select the keyboard from the list to pair. If prompted, confirm any pairing code on the keyboard. [p0176]

- If the TV doesn’t list any Bluetooth devices at all, contact support. [p0241]  
- If pairing is unstable: keep the keyboard close, reduce interference, and make sure it’s charged. [p0241]

Would you like steps to disconnect or remove a keyboard?
reference_answer: Open Settings > General > External Device Manager > Input Device Manager > Bluetooth Device List. If the keyboard is not detected, move it close to the TV and select Refresh so that the TV scans again. The function may not be supported depending on the model or region.

question: The remote control does nothing when I press the buttons.
answer:
Here are the checks to get your Smart Tech TV responding to the remote again. Follow them in order:

1) Confirm Voice Guide and “Learn TV Remote” (helps verify buttons are recognized)
- Turn on Voice Guide: Settings > General > Accessibility > Voice Guide [p0103][p0169].
- Start Learn TV Remote: Settings > General > Accessibility > Learn TV Remote. Press some remote buttons; the TV should speak each button’s name. To return, press the button twice; to exit, press and hold the button [p0169].
- If the TV announces button names here, the remote is working and the issue may be in the current app/screen.

2) Use the e‑Manual’s Accessibility Guidance to test safely
- Open e‑Manual: press E‑MANUAL on the standard remote; or Smart Tech Hub > Settings > Support > Open e‑Manual [p0103].
- In the e‑Manual, open Accessibility Guidance > Learn TV Remote. While viewing this section, pressing remote buttons won’t control the TV; it only reads the button names aloud (useful to confirm the remote is detected) [p0103].

3) Try channel, volume, and on‑screen number pad actions (to confirm response)
- Channel change: Use the right protruding button; push up/down. The TV should announce the new channel each time [p0143].
- Volume: Use the left protruding VOL button; push up/down. The TV should announce the new volume level [p0143].
- Virtual numeric pad (Smart Tech Remote): Press the button to bring up the on‑screen numbers; use left/right to pick numbers, then Done. Voice Guide should say “virtual numeric pad …” when it appears [p0143].

If none of the above steps cause any spoken feedback or on‑screen changes, the manual passages don’t provide further remote troubleshooting (like batteries or pairing). I can hand this over to a human colleague to help with deeper checks and possible repair options. Would you like me to connect you?
reference_answer: Replace the batteries, point the remote at the sensor with nothing in between, and remove the protective stickers from the sensors. Pair the remote again by pointing it at the sensor and pressing and holding both pairing buttons for 3 seconds or more. In the meantime use the buttons on the TV or the Smart Tech Home app. Contact support if it still fails.
must_include: replace the batteries; point the remote at the sensor; remove protective stickers; pair again by holding both pairing buttons for 3 seconds; contact support
unknown_menu_paths: Settings > General > Accessibility > Voice Guide [p0103][p0169] | Settings > Support > Open e‑Manual [p0103]

question: I switch to the HDMI input of my game console but the screen stays black.
answer:
Here are all the checks to fix a black screen after switching to your console’s HDMI input:

1) Confirm the right HDMI port
- Press Source and select the exact port your console uses (HDMI1/HDMI2, etc.) [p0239], [p0006].

2) Power and reseat connections
- Turn the console on.
- Unplug and firmly replug the HDMI cable at both the console and TV ends. Then try again [p0239].

3) Try different port and cable
- Move the cable to another HDMI port on the TV.
- If possible, try a different High‑Speed HDMI cable [p0239].

4) Check HDMI UHD Color for UHD/HDR consoles
- Go to Settings > General > External Device Manager > HDMI UHD Color and set it to On for that HDMI port.
- If the screen stays black, set it to Off and test again [p0239].

5) Adjust the console’s output resolution
- Set the console to a supported resolution (e.g., 1080p). Then unplug and reconnect (power‑cycle) the console and try again [p0239].

6) Game Mode (optional)
- You can enable game mode for best performance at Settings > General > External Device Manager > Game Mode Settings > Game Mode. Note: Game Mode switches Picture and Sound to Game automatically and is not needed to restore the image if there’s no signal [p0029].

If the TV shows no picture from any device on any HDMI port after these steps, please let me know and I can hand this over to a human colleague for further assistance [p0239].
reference_answer: Select the right port in Source, push the HDMI cable in fully and switch the device on. Try another HDMI port or a High-Speed HDMI cable. For a UHD player change Settings > General > External Device Manager > HDMI UHD Color, and set the output resolution of the device to a supported value. Contact support if no device shows a picture on any port.
must_include: select the right port in Source; HDMI cable fully inserted and device on; another port or cable; HDMI UHD Color for a UHD player; contact support if no port works

question: Where do I set a sleep timer and how long can it be?
answer:
You can set it in two places:

1) Full menu path
- Go to: Settings > General > System Manager > Time > Sleep Timer.
- You can set a countdown to automatically turn the TV off after up to 180 minutes. [p0121][p0067]

2) Quick access from Home Screen
- Press Home, move to the left menu, select Sleep Timer, then press Select to choose the countdown. For a specific shutoff time, press the up button and choose Set Up Off Timer. Note: Sleep Timer is a countdown (up to 180 minutes); Off Timer turns off at a specific time. [p0067]

If you only need the maximum duration: it’s 180 minutes. [p0121][p0067]
reference_answer: Open Settings > General > System Manager > Time > Sleep Timer. The TV then switches itself off after the time you set, up to 180 minutes.
must_include: Settings > General > System Manager > Time > Sleep Timer; up to 180 minutes

question: My TV turns itself on at night. Why?
answer:
It’s usually a wake feature or connected device. Try these checks:

1) Disable phone wake
- Go to: Settings > General > Network > Expert Settings > Power On with Mobile
- Turn it Off [p0243]

2) Disable HDMI-CEC wake
- Go to: Settings > General > External Device Manager > Anynet+ (HDMI-CEC)
- Turn it Off (some HDMI devices can power the TV on) [p0243]

3) Remove schedules
- Open: Live TV > Schedule Manager
- Delete any viewing/recording schedules you don’t need [p0243]

4) Check automations
- Ensure no Smart Tech Home automation or Smart Tech Voice routine is set to turn the TV on [p0243]

Fix approach:
- Turn these features off, then re-enable them one at a time, waiting a night after each change to see which one causes the wake-up. Re-enable “Power On with Mobile” only if you want phone control [p0243].

If the TV still wakes up with all of them off, please contact support for further diagnosis [p0243].
reference_answer: Switch off Power On with Mobile (Settings > General > Network > Expert Settings) and Anynet+ (HDMI-CEC) in External Device Manager, delete schedules you do not need in Live TV > Schedule Manager, and check Smart Tech Home automations and voice routines. Switch the functions on again one at a time to find the cause. Contact support if it wakes up with all of them off.
must_include: switch off Power On with Mobile and Anynet+ (HDMI-CEC); delete unneeded schedules; check Smart Tech Home automations and voice routines; test one at a time

question: The TV says Weak or No Signal and some channels are missing.
answer:
Here are the checks to fix “Weak or No Signal” and missing channels:

1) Cable and source
- Ensure the antenna/cable connection is firmly plugged into the TV.
- If using a cable/satellite box, also check the box’s output and that the TV is on the correct source/input. [p0246]

2) Check signal strength
- Go to Settings > Support > Self Diagnosis > Signal Information (digital channels only) and review the signal level/quality. [p0246]

3) Rescan channels (antenna only)
- If you use an antenna (not a cable/satellite box), run Settings > Broadcasting > Auto Program to scan again. Note: this replaces the saved channel list, including Favorites. Do not use Auto Program with a cable/satellite box. [p0246][p0117]

4) Consider conditions that weaken signal
- Bad weather, a defective splitter, or a misaligned antenna can weaken the signal and cause breakup or missing channels. [p0246]
- Compression on some broadcasts (especially fast sports/action) can look distorted even with a good signal; prefer HD channels/programs for better quality. [p0117]

If the signal remains weak after these steps, ask an antenna installer to align the antenna and scan again, or contact your cable/satellite provider. We can also hand you over to a human colleague if you’d like more help. [p0246][p0117]
reference_answer: Check the antenna cable, open Settings > Support > Self Diagnosis > Signal Information (digital channels only) to see the strength, and if you use an antenna (not a cable or satellite box) run Settings > Broadcasting > Auto Program to scan again; the scan replaces the saved channel list. Align the antenna if needed. Contact your cable or satellite provider or an antenna installer if the signal stays weak.
must_include: check the antenna cable; Signal Information; Auto Program only with an antenna (it replaces the channel list); antenna installer or provider if the signal stays weak
